brands.evidence: I’d pick Monzo if you mostly pay by card and often split bills.
I’d pick Starling if you regularly pay in cash or use cash machines abroad.

client_claims.text: Monzo offers a current account with no monthly fee.
client_claims.note: A free plan exists alongside the paid plans.

client_claims.text: Neither bank charges a fee for card purchases abroad.
client_claims.note: Monzo charges no fee on card spending abroad.

client_claims.text: Outside the UK and EEA, free Monzo gives £200 of withdrawals per rolling 30 days, then charges 3% on the excess.
Free Monzo charges £1 each time you pay in cash, whether at a PayPoint or Post Office.
client_claims.note: Cash deposit fees are not covered by the facts.

client_claims.text: You can split a single dinner bill or keep a running total for groceries and trips. Friends can join by link without opening a Monzo account, and the app can remind them to pay.
client_claims.note: Split feature details are not covered by the facts.

client_claims.text: In the August 2026 independent Great Britain service survey, 79% of Monzo customers would recommend it, versus 76% for Starling, ranking first and second.
client_claims.note: The facts give an NPS of 76, not this survey's figure.
